newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican business magnate Peralta dies at 82.
newsitem.headline: Mexican business magnate Peralta dies at 82.

text.p: Business magnate and baseball fanatic Alejo Peralta y Diaz Ceballos, one of Mexico's richest men, died from a heart attack on Tuesday at the age of 80, the official news agency Notimex said.

Peralta was the patriarch of a family whose fortune was first made in copper electrical products and later branched out into products like cellular phones through a 48 percent stake in publicly traded Grupo Iusacell.
Iusacell's rapid stock price rise in the early 1990s made the family into paper billionaires, but the company management was eventually taken over by partner Bell Atlantic Corp.
Peralta's son Carlos was also publicly criticised after allegations of dubious business dealings and tax evasion.

The family company Grupo Iusa retains interests in construction, automotive equipment and financial services but patriarch Alejo was better remembered by most of his countrymen for his role in expanding baseball in Mexico.
A past founder-owner of the Tigres (Tigers) and Aztecas (Aztecs) baseball teams in the 1950s, Peralta was also a force behind the creation of the Mexican Baseball Academy.
The Mexican Baseball League declared a day of national mourning for Peralta and suspended all games.
"Today at 11 o'clock in the morning, the Great Tiger said farewell to us," the League said in a statement.
Among his other achievements, Peralta also headed the National Polytechnic Institute and in 1958 set up Latin America's first cultural public television channel.
Born in May 1916 in the eastern city of Puebla, Peralta is survived by his wife and four children.
